abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) and Multiple System Atrophy (MSA) are progressive synucleinopathies characterized by widespread molecular alterations across neuronal and glial populations. While brain tissue provides direct insight into disease mechanisms, liquid biopsies, particularly extracellular vesicles (EVs) in plasma, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and urine, offer a minimally invasive avenue for clinical diagnosis and monitoring. However, the extent to which cell-type-specific brain transcriptional changes translate into detectable circulating protein signatures remains unclear. Here, we present a comprehensive multi-omics meta-analysis integrating eight human post-mortem brain single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) datasets with eight circulating proteomic datasets. We uniformly reprocessed and analyzed over 1 million nuclei, spanning ~20,000 protein-coding genes across four broadly defined disease-relevant brain regions from 171 individuals alongside ~8,000 liquid biopsy proteins from over 400 individuals. We resolved cell-type-specific differentially expressed genes (DEGs) across dopaminergic neurons, microglia, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes alongside disease-specific differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in peripheral biofluids. Mapping brain DEGs onto liquid biopsy proteomes revealed that ~25% of brain DEGs were detectable as biofluid DEPs in at least one dataset, while multi-cohort filtering prioritized 32 unique recurrent cross-omic biomarkers. These include concordantly regulated markers of complement and glial reactivity (C1QB, C3, CHI3L1), neurotrophic and neuropeptide signaling (IGFBP5, NRP1, SST), lipid metabolism (LPL, APOC1), proteostasis (HSP90B1), and cytoskeletal/extracellular matrix remodeling (MMP2, PLOD1), alongside inversely regulated chaperones and synaptic/vascular factors (HSP90AA1, CAMK2A, VWF). Furthermore, cross-omic protein-protein interaction networks converged on pathways governing chaperone-mediated protein folding, ubiquitin-proteasome degradation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and SNARE-mediated vesicular transport. Ultimately, this integrative atlas links brain cell-type-specific transcriptomic dysregulation to accessible EV cargo, providing a scalable framework for mechanistically informed liquid biopsies in neurodegeneration.
